title: Supported-Hom evaluation and cocycle normalization data
statement:
Use the small-site size convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let C be a category with object universe u+1 and morphism universe u, J a Grothendieck topology, A a commutative ring in universe u+1, and Sh_A(J) the category of sheaves of A-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with sheafification and enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. Fix a terminal object T, an arrow j:W→T, an A-module sheaf B, and a map ρ:A_J→B from the constant rank-one module [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put S(M)=ker(M(T)→M(W)), the supported-sections functor [def-pur-support-cohomology], and view its values as abelian groups when comparing with Hom. Use the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its bounded-below subcategory [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and bounded-below degreewise injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

Define supported-Hom cocycle-normalization data to consist of (1) an additive natural isomorphism θ:Hom(B,−)≅S(−), with kernel inclusion sending θ_M(f) to the evaluation at 1 of ρ followed by f under the constant-sheaf/terminal-sections adjunction; (2) additive equivalences χ_{F,a}:H^a(RS(F))≃Hom(B[0],F[a]) for every bounded-below F and a∈Z, natural in F; and (3) the following cocycle equation. For every quasi-isomorphism e:K→I of bounded-below cochain complexes with I degreewise injective, and every cycle x in S(I) of degree a, there is a unique f:B→I^a whose θ-image is the image of x under the cycles inclusion. This f is closed, and χ sends the class of x, transported through the canonical derived-unit and resolution comparisons to H^a(RS(QK)), to the localized single-complex cocycle map B[0]→QI[a] followed by the inverse resolution comparison to QK[a]. The localization uses the standard single-complex Hom cocycle with differential f d=0 and the canonical quotient-to-derived comparison.

For such data N, define ConeAgreement(N) to mean that for every bounded-below degreewise injective I, the actual kernel inclusion κ:S(I)→I(T), after forgetting A to abelian groups, has zero composite with the restriction r:I(T)→I(W), and that both the canonical closed-cone lift κ:S(I)→Cone(r)[−1] and its composite with the termwise evaluation isomorphism θ_I are quasi-isomorphisms. In the standard shifted mapping-cone coordinates this lift sends s to (0,s), equivalently (s,0) in the relative-cone coordinates of [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology]. This is a predicate on data, not an assertion that such data exist.

For any morphism i:Z→X of schemes [def-pc-scheme], on their small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] also define the canonical constant restriction A_X→i_*A_Z [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] as the adjunction transpose under i^*⊣i_* [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] of the canonical constant-sheaf identification i^*A_X≅A_Z. No closed-immersion or purity hypothesis is part of these plain definitions.
